articles.title: The Batman 2 is delayed to 2027, but Mickey 17’s release date is moving up
articles.summary: The Batman Part II has been delayed until October 1st 2027, Warner Bros. has announced. An unnamed film starring Tom Cruise will its place on October 2nd, 2026.
articles.body: If you’ve been waiting patiently to see how Matt Reeves’ story for The Batman continues once the reboot’s sequel arrives, you’ll have to wait a little longer. It was once set to open October 2nd, 2026, after an initial delay caused by the Hollywood writers’ strike derailed Warner Bros. plans to release it in 2025, but the studio has now announced that it’s pushing The Batman Part II even further back to October 1st, 2027, according to Variety. It appears the most recent shift could be strategic. Variety adds that Warner Bros. has rushed to fill that October 2nd, 2026, slot with an unnamed film featuring Tom Cruise and directed by Alejandro G. Iñárritu. While that sucks for fans of the bat, one nice consolation is news that Bong Joon-Ho’s Mickey 17 is coming even sooner than expected; it is now scheduled for March 7th, 2025, after delays of its own caused the original 2024 release to slip. Mickey 17 stars Robert Pattinson (who also plays Bruce Wayne in The Batman Part II) and is directly inspired by the Edward Ashton novel Mickey7, which follows a willingly and literally disposable employee through his many doors of death. Also starring in the film are Steven Yeun, Naomi Ackie, Toni Collette, Mark Ruffalo, and Thomas Turgoose. Warner Bros. reportedly swapped its release date with Ryan Coogler’s Sinners, which now opens April 18th, to give Mickey 17 more time on Imax screens.

articles.title: Ajay Devgn's 'Drishyam 3' makes Rs 273 crore, approximately $28.4 million in its opening weekend, beats Tom Cruise's 'Digger' which has made Rs $ 20 million
articles.summary: Indian films have occasionally made a strong impact at the global box office, but very few have managed to finish ahead of major Hollywood releases during
articles.body: Indian films have occasionally made a strong impact at the global box office, but very few have managed to finish ahead of major Hollywood releases during the same weekend. Films such as ‘RRR’, ‘Jawan’ and ‘Kalki 2898 AD’ have made their presence felt internationally, while ‘Dhurandhar: The Revenge’ also emerged as a major global success. However, Ajay Devgn-starrer ‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’ has now achieved a new milestone by finishing ahead of a Tom Cruise film in a direct box-office clash.The third instalment of the ‘Drishyam’ franchise has emerged as the second highest-grossing film worldwide over its opening weekend. The film had a powerful start in India, collecting Rs 62 crore net on its opening day. It maintained its momentum over the weekend and ended its first three days with Rs 176.50 crore net, translating to around Rs 211.80 crore or $22 million gross.The film also made its presence felt in overseas markets. While its opening in the US and Canada was not as explosive as its performance in India, it still managed to put up a respectable number. According to Comscore and Box Office Mojo, ‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’ earned $2.7 million across North America from slightly more than 500 theatres.Its performance in other international territories has been stronger, with markets across Europe and the Gulf contributing more than $3.4 million. By Sunday, the film had accumulated an estimated $28.4 million, or approximately Rs 273 crore, worldwide.That figure placed ‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’ at No. 2 globally for the weekend. The only film ahead of it was Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson's erotic thriller ‘Verity’, which registered a massive $62.6 million worldwide, including $32 million from the US and Canada.More significantly, ‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’ finished ahead of Tom Cruise's ‘Digger’, which also arrived in cinemas during the weekend. The film marked Cruise's return to director-backed projects after a series of action-heavy outings but opened to around $20 million worldwide, falling short of the Ajay Devgn-starrer.The Hindi film also finished ahead of another major Hollywood release, Brad Pitt's ‘Heart of the Beast’. The latter collected $28 million in its second weekend, placing it third globally. ‘Resident Evil’ rounded off the top five with an estimated weekend worldwide collection of $24.5 million.‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’ brings back Ajay Devgn as Vijay Salgaonkar, alongside Tabu, Shriya Saran, Rajat Kapoor, Ishita Dutta, Mrunal Jadhav and Kamlesh Sawant. Saurabh Shukla also returns from ‘Drishyam 2’ in a cameo, while Jaideep Ahlawat and Prakash Raj are the new additions to the cast.Written and directed by Abhishek Pathak, the film hit theatres on October 2, a significant date for the franchise. Unlike the first two Hindi films, which were remakes of the Malayalam ‘Drishyam’ films, the third instalment follows an original story and takes the franchise in a new direction.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Pedro Piqueras explica por qué la legislatura de Pedro Sánchez ha sido “atroz” y expone la razón principal del adelanto electoral: “Se ha quedado solo”
articles.standfirst: El colaborador de ‘Mañaneros 360’ responsabiliza a los partidos de derecha por los “insultos”
articles.summary: El colaborador de ‘Mañaneros 360’ responsabiliza a los partidos de derecha por los “insultos”
articles.body: Ya es una realidad. El próximo 29 de noviembre, España tendrá elecciones generales. Pedro Sánchez las ha convocado este mismo lunes 5 y, ahora, todos los partidos se preparan para meses de crispación, debate y programas políticos. En ‘Mañaneros 360’ han contado con Pedro Piqueras para hablar de la decisión del presidente del Gobierno y las razones del adelanto electoral. A su juicio, era algo necesario porque era “una legislatura que ya no tiene mucho sentido seguir”. Sobre los motivos que han terminado provocando que las elecciones generales se adelanten un año, tampoco tiene dudas: “Le han fallado los apoyos en un momento crucial, como era el de la vivienda”. Pedro Piqueras detalla que, a su modo de ver, nunca se pudo considerar a Junts un aliado fiel para el actual Gobierno: “Ha sido ventajista en el sentido de conseguir acuerdos relacionados con la amnistía y otros asuntos para Cataluña, pero, en los momentos decisivos, ha negociado muy fuerte”. También ha querido responsabilizar a los partidos de derecha por la “polarización” actual que vive la sociedad española: “Creo que para el presidente del Gobierno ha sido una legislatura atroz, han sido tres años de polarización. Es más culpa de la derecha, por los insultos que se lanzaban contra Pedro Sánchez, las polémicas parlamentarias, a veces de una dureza…”. Asimismo, reconoce que se han dicho cosas en los mitines o en el Congreso de los Diputados que a él mismo le ruborizaría decir en televisión. “Era una legislatura que tenía que terminar cuanto antes. El presidente del Gobierno se ha quedado un poco solo y yo creo que, desde mi punto de vista, no tenía más remedio”, zanja Piqueras en RTVE sobre este asunto.

articles.title: In 2023, Leonardo DiCaprio and Jeff Bezos teamed up to protect the Amazon rainforest; $200 million commitment brought their nonprofits together
articles.summary: In 2023, Leonardo DiCaprio and Jeff Bezos announced a $200 million partnership to protect the Amazon rainforest through their nonprofit organizations. The initiative aims for zero deforestation and the protection of biodiversity.
articles.body: Back in 2023, ‘One Battle After Another’ star Leonardo DiCaprio paired up with American businessman Jeff Bezos, who is also known as the second-richest person on Earth. The two unlikely forces came together to fight for the Amazon rainforest, which has been depleting in size and quality for a variety of reasons.When Leonardo DiCaprio and Jeff Bezos worked together on raising funds for the Amazon rainforestIn July 2023, as per reports shared online by the Associated Press, DiCaprio and Bezos' nonprofit organizations collaborated to launch a dedicated fund for the Amazon rainforest, along with Vice President Lauren Sánchez. They committed over USD 200 million through the Protect Our Planet (POP) Challenge for the cause.The pledge focused on supporting Brazil's environmental goals, which included achieving zero deforestation in the Amazon and safeguarding protected areas and Indigenous areas as well. The funds were meant to be invested in things like municipal and national programs that may help achieve zero illegal deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon. Not only that, but the funding was also established to reinforce and help with physical monitoring, infrastructure, and ecological management of existing national parks.At the time, DiCaprio shared a statement about the collaboration between him and Bezos, saying, “We are inspired by Brazil’s ambitious goals for protecting the Amazon, one of the most important places for wildlife on the planet, and are thrilled to be able to support these efforts through the Protecting Our Planet Challenge.”One of the representatives of Bezos’ nonprofit, Cristián Samper, also explained at the time that “Amazon is critical for the future of global biodiversity and climate, and we welcome the commitment from President Lula and the Government of Brazil to protect it. We are pleased to support the designation and management of protected areas and Indigenous territories as a key part of the strategy to reduce deforestation, along with new economic models of development based on the conservation and sustainable use of the forest.”Leonardo DiCaprio and Jeff Bezos extended the project and launched the Phoenix Species ProjectThey invested additional money into the project to start a brand new branch that mainly focused on preventing the extinction of 100 of the world's most critically endangered species. Some of the priority species that were named in the program included the golden-crowned sifaka (Madagascar lemur), Malayan pangolins, and the pink land iguana in the Galápagos.The main objective of the program was to move away from short-term goals and instead invest their funding into sustained multi-year habitat protection and species breeding/restoration programs to ensure that these species do not cease to exist.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ star Isaiah Washington reveals his wife died more than a year ago
articles.summary: Former “Grey’s Anatomy” star Isaiah Washington revealed in an Instagram post that his wife of 29 years, Jenisa Washington — who also went by Jenisa Garland — died more than a year ago.
articles.body: Former “Grey’s Anatomy” star Isaiah Washington revealed in an Instagram post over the weekend that his wife of 29 years, Jenisa Washington, died more than a year ago. Appearing to address speculation, Washington said that “the rumors are true” and that his wife — who also went by Jenisa Garland — had “collapsed suddenly” in May 2025 and died on June 9, 2025. “It came as a huge shock to me and our entire family. She succumbed to a massive hemorrhagic stroke and never recovered,” he wrote Saturday. “Listen, y’all…some headaches are not just headaches or migraines, they can be much worse and a warning sign. Get a brain scan if you can and take those headaches seriously.” A hemorrhagic stroke occurs when a blood vessel in the brain bursts, causing bleeding in or around the brain, according to the National Library of Medicine’s MedlinePlus. The bleeding increases pressure inside the skull and damages brain tissue. Common causes include an aneurysm, high blood pressure, head trauma or arteriovenous malformation. According to MedlinePlus, symptoms can include a sudden severe headache, sudden dizziness or trouble walking, sudden confusion, and sudden numbness or weakness in the face. “She has been gone 16 months now, but she left 3 incredibly amazing children behind to continue her legacy,” the actor said. Washington didn’t say why he waited over a year to announce her death but suggested that she may not have wanted the information made public. “I don’t know if this is an appropriate post, because Jenisa Washington was extremely private, but I guess I just have to be reprimanded from her on the other side,” he wrote. Celebrities including Viola Davis, Loni Love, Michael Beach, Tichina Arnold and Neil Brown Jr. offered their condolences to Washington. Washington appeared on “Grey’s Anatomy” as Dr. Preston Burke but was fired in 2007 after he used a homophobic slur against a co-star. He later apologized.

articles.title: Chris Rock Says He Refused to Pay for a Lawyer for His Wrongfully Accused Friend’s Brother: ‘I Had the Means to Help Him and I Didn’t’
articles.summary: The actor opened up about the situation in a new interview with ‘The New York Times’
articles.body:
Chris Rock opened up about a personal experience in his life denying his friend's brother, Roger Logan, a lawyer after he was wrongfully accused of murder

The comedian said his decision "still f---s with me"

Rock is currently promoting Misty Green , his new directorial project in theaters Oct. 9

Chris Rock got candid in a new interview about a hard decision he made in his personal life.

The actor, 61, joined The New York Times ' The Interview series where he opened up about his new movie, Misty Green , and weighed in on the subject of progressiveness and its impact on celebrities. When asked about who deserves forgiveness and why, in the context of what Rock describes as "canceled all-stars," he shared an anecdote from his own life.

"Hey, man, I'm Black. When you're Black, white people believe every accusation is a conviction," he began.

Rock went on to give an example of someone he knew who was wrongfully accused.

"A guy named Roger Logan , who I grew up with and was one of my best friends' brothers, went to jail for 19 years for a murder he didn't commit," Rock said. "And here's the weird thing: His brother used to plead with me to pay for a lawyer for Roger, and I never did it. I always had a no-lawyer thing."

Rock said that he had no issue paying for people's mortgage or education, but when it came to lawyers, he took a step back because "it's so open-ended."

Per the NYT , Logan eventually reached a $3.75 million settlement with New York City over his wrongful conviction and settled with New York State for $2.975 million.

"And it still f---s with me. I had the means to help him, and I didn't," he admitted. "I don't know if we could've got him out or not, but still. So all that to say, I'm Black, Black men get accused of s--- they didn't do all the time, every day. We let Black men out of jail and go: 'Whoops! That Black guy just did 30 years — too bad.' "

"So to answer your question, hopefully I don't get accused of anything, but it's real when people get accused of things, and you better be real sure they did it," Rock concluded.

The actor added that he himself was in a police lineup "two, three times."

"In Bed-Stuy, and you're minding your business and you get swooped up. And now you're in a police lineup," he explained of his experience in the neighborhood growing up. "And you've seen enough cop movies to know that behind that window is a person — could be a man, but probably a woman — and if she points at you, your whole life's over."

Rock is currently promoting his latest directorial project, Misty Green , which stars Rosalind Eleazar as the titular character who is fighting to reclaim her career years after her Hollywood breakthrough.

The film first premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on Sept. 12 before making its debut at the New York Film Festival two weeks later.

Rock previously opened up to PEOPLE about working with his younger daughter, Zahra , 22, on the movie, in which she has a small role.

" It was fun to direct her ," Rock told PEOPLE at TIFF, adding that it made him think back to days he spent alongside his own father: "I used to work with my dad a lot. My dad drove a truck...but occasionally I would have to watch somebody tell my dad what to do, and that kind of stuck with me. So it was nice for my daughter to come in this atmosphere where her dad's the boss."

articles.title: In 2015, Josh Hartnett sold his US homes; years later, the Verity star made a Hampshire farm his permanent home with wife Tamsin Egerton and 4 kids
articles.summary: Josh Hartnett may have spent the early part of his career as one of Hollywood’s most recognisable leading men, but his life away from the cameras looks
articles.body: Josh Hartnett may have spent the early part of his career as one of Hollywood’s most recognisable leading men, but his life away from the cameras looks remarkably different. The actor, known for films including Pearl Harbor, Black Hawk Down and Oppenheimer, now lives with his wife, British actress Tamsin Egerton, and their four children in the Hampshire countryside in England.At the centre of Hartnett’s quieter life is the family’s small farm. Rather than a sprawling celebrity estate, he has described it as a “tiny little farm”, where everyday family life unfolds alongside a collection of animals. In a recent appearance on the UK show This Morning, Hartnett gave a glimpse into just how busy the household can get. “We’ve got a little farm, tiny little farm,” Hartnett said. “A lot of animals, we have four kids, so it’s busy. “My life is my family life, and then every once in a while I come out and do something like this, which is such an anomaly for me.”A farm filled with animalsHartnett’s Hampshire home is not just about having a quieter address. The actor has previously spoken about the animals that are part of the family’s everyday routine.A report described mornings at the property as involving his four children as well as a dog, several guinea pigs, chickens and a small group of pygmy goats. Hartnett has a particular fondness for the goats and described them as exceptionally affectionate.The actor has also spoken about the simple pleasures of rural life, including feeding the goats and spending time outdoors with his children. The family’s move to the English countryside has allowed him to build a routine that is considerably removed from the intensity of his earlier Hollywood years.His life revolves around his familyHartnett and Egerton have four children, although the couple have deliberately kept their children’s names and most personal details away from the public eye. Their first three children were born in 2015, 2017 and 2019, while Hartnett confirmed in 2024 that they had welcomed a fourth child.The actor has repeatedly made it clear that being present for his family is a priority. In his recent interviews, he has spoken about how his family has helped him feel more grounded and comfortable with the attention that comes with his profession.His wife, Tamsin Egerton, has also largely stayed away from the spotlight despite having her own acting career. The couple have been together for years and quietly married in 2021.Why Josh Hartnett left Los AngelesHartnett’s decision to settle in England was not simply a change of scenery. At the height of his fame, he deliberately stepped back from the Hollywood machine because he did not want his career to become his entire identity. In a 2024 interview with The Guardian, he explained, “Hollywood is more than a place, it’s like a state of mind.”He continued, “If you’re around people who are constantly talking about the movie business, your life is going to be pretty much one note. And I’ve never wanted that.”Hartnett also had little affection for the practical realities of living in Los Angeles, adding, “I just never really vibed with L.A. because I’m not a big fan of sitting in the car all day.”The actor had reached a point where he was being offered major blockbuster roles, including Superman, but chose not to follow the conventional path to franchise stardom. He later explained that he did not want his life to be consumed by his profession.From Hollywood heart-throb to countryside lifeHartnett became a major star following films such as Pearl Harbor and Black Hawk Down, but instead of continually chasing bigger projects, he gradually chose a more private life and more selective work.His retreat from Hollywood did not mean he stopped acting. In recent years, he has appeared in projects including Christopher Nolan’s Oppenheimer, the Netflix series Black Mirror and M. Night Shyamalan’s Trap. He also appeared in The Bear and is currently promoting the thriller Verity.His approach to work has changed, however. The actor has spoken about choosing projects that interest him while keeping his family life at the centre of his priorities.For Hartnett, the contrast between his public career and private home could hardly be greater. One side involves film sets, premieres and press tours; the other involves four children, chickens, guinea pigs, a dog and his beloved pygmy goats on a small farm in the English countryside.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Ms Rachel rips celebrities who do 'nothing during a genocide'
articles.summary: Ms. Rachel's Instagram post takes aim at celebrities she says are "doing nothing" amid the Gaza conflict
articles.body: Children's YouTube entertainer Ms. Rachel took another swipe at high-profile celebrities who have remained silent on Gaza in a social media post on Sunday, saying she is unimpressed by fame when public figures are "doing nothing" during what she has repeatedly called a genocide. "Do you want to meet insert huge celeb? Me: No," Rachel Griffin Accurso, known as Ms. Rachel, said in an Instagram post. "I don’t fan girl over someone who is doing nothing during a genocide." MOMS FOR LIBERTY CO-FOUNDER WARNS PARENTS ABOUT MS RACHEL’S POLITICAL ACTIVISM, ‘NOT MR ROGERS’ The post came less than a week after Campaign Against Antisemitism criticized Accurso in a statement to Fox News Digital over her declaration that she would not work with "privileged" people who stay silent about Gaza. A spokesperson from Campaign Against Antisemitism said that her standard amounted to an exclusionary political test. "Ms. Rachel’s comments on who she is willing to work with are patently hypocritical," the spokesperson said. "Acting as an adjudicator is a privileged position in and of itself, and subjecting people to political purity tests is by definition exclusionary. One would have thought that someone who has admitted to having – apparently accidentally – liked a comment online saying 'Free America from the Jews', Ms. Rachel would be taking care to avoid these sorts of topics entirely." "Evidently the temptation to ostracize those with differing views on the war in Gaza, many of whom will be Jews, is too strong for her to resist," they continued. MACKLEMORE DONATES $1M TO PALESTINIAN AID ORGANIZATIONS AFTER ED SHEERAN TOUR FALLOUT Accurso's expanding political profile had also drawn pushback from parents. Washington Examiner contributor, author and homeschooling mother Bethany Mandel accused Accurso of amplifying what she called a Hamas narrative, telling Fox News Digital last week that the children's entertainer had become an influential messenger about the war. "She is serving as their mouthpiece for a lot of Americans, not just children and not just the adults that follow her," Mandel said. Accurso did not identify the "huge celeb" she may have been referencing in her post. In the caption, however, she said she would still speak directly with prominent people if she believed she could persuade them to use their platforms. "I'd have a conversation with someone with a massive platform any day to try and convince them to speak out. (And I have)," Accurso said. MS RACHEL DEFENDS HER ACTIVISM BY POINTING TO MISTER ROGERS' POLITICAL LEGACY ON CHILDREN'S TV The post was the latest in a series of challenges Accurso has issued to celebrities concerning Gaza. Last month, she pledged to match rapper Macklemore's $1 million donation to Palestinian aid organizations and called on "every wealthy White celebrity" to do the same. During a separate appearance on comedian Ilana Glazer's "It's Open" podcast, she targeted celebrities she described as too famous to be canceled. Accurso questioned why celebrities with secure careers would not publicly advocate for civilians in Gaza during the podcast appearance. "If you are so famous, and you’re uncancellable, and you’re so famous and you won’t even say like, 'Kids in Gaza should have schools, people in Gaza should have hospitals.' Like you won't say something so basic and like why can't you risk something to help save lives?" Accurso said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The continued political activism comes as Accurso's media empire continues to grow. Accurso has more than 21 million YouTube subscribers and has donated roughly $22,500 to Democratic and progressive candidates since 2024. Her brand has also secured partnerships with Netflix, Penguin Random House and Spin Master.

articles.title: Mark Ruffalo threatens to 'hulk out' at Trump, GOP over voting rights at NYC event
articles.summary: Mark Ruffalo threatened to "hulk out" at a NYC rally targeting Trump and the Republican Party, urging Democrats to fight back in midterm elections.
articles.body: Actor Mark Ruffalo threatened to "hulk out" at a New York City event on Sunday in an expletive-filled rant targeting President Donald Trump and the Republican Party, who, he argued, were trying to stop Democrats "from taking our country back." During a "Hands Off Our Vote" event, Ruffalo sounded the alarm and said Republicans were trying to "steal" the midterm elections, according to Variety. "We got to get this dumba---, fool a--, tired a--, lame a--, duck a-- out of office. We got to make him a lame duck! We have to stop his policies now. Another two years of this, and who knows what he’ll be doing? He’s calling to throw Democrats out of the country," Ruffalo said, according to the outlet. "And he means it! The guy means everything he says. I know we’re all tired, we are so tired, but we can’t give up now ... They’re going to try and stop us from taking our country back, and we’re not going to let ’em. Trump, we’re not letting you! Hands off our f---ing vote!" Ruffalo said. MARK RUFFALO FIRES BACK AT PARAMOUNT OVER 'APPALLING' ANTISEMITISM ACCUSATION TIED TO ELLISON MERGER CRITICISM "I’m going to hulk out. You won’t like me when I’m angry," he said, after a member of the audience cheered him on, referencing his portrayal of Marvel Cinematic Universe's "The Incredible Hulk," Variety reported. "Hey, I’m still here! They thought I was out for the count — I’m still here, I’m still playing the Hulk," Ruffalo said. "We can’t hide. We have to be together, and we have to fight for each other and we have to be brave. Our time to be brave is coming, I’m telling you brothers and sisters," Ruffalo said, according to the outlet. "They’re going to do everything they can to keep us in our homes. They’re going to do everything they can to make us feel small. They’re going to do everything they can to make us feel lost, to make it feel inevitable. It’s not inevitable! We’re inevitable — the truth is inevitable," he said. CLINTON-APPOINTED JUDGE TRIGGERS APPEAL AFTER BLOCKING KEY VOTER CITIZENSHIP LAW The RNC fired back at Ruffalo in a statement to Fox News Digital. "Mark Ruffalo is clearly stuck in La La Land. In the real world, voter ID and proof of citizenship are wildly popular, and noncitizens keep turning up on voter rolls," Ally Triolo, the RNC's election integrity communications director, told Fox News Digital in a statement. "Democrats fight commonsense safeguards because they believe they can't win when Republicans make it easier to vote and harder to cheat," Triolo said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE The White House also shredded Ruffalo for his comments, saying the actor had "Trump Derangement Syndrome." "Mark Ruffalo is a no-talent loser who has totally beclowned himself by spewing disgusting lies and spreading hate due to his severe and incurable case of Trump Derangement Syndrome. He is so devoid of actual talent that nobody with any commonsense would ever watch him unless it was to laugh at his miserable failures," White House spokesman Davis Ingle told Fox News Digital. Ruffalo blasted the outcome of the long-running fight over Paramount's $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery last week after a federal judge cleared the Hollywood megadeal to move forward Wednesday. Ruffalo, who had been one of the most vocal Hollywood opponents of the merger, called the outcome "incredibly disappointing." "This merger will stifle creativity, weaken free speech, and cost people their jobs – it is a bad deal for this country and should never have been approved," Ruffalo wrote in a post on X.CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "This is an incredibly disappointing outcome for the hundreds of thousands of us who stood up to block it, but it's also not the end," he continued. "This grassroots movement isn't going to fade away and neither is our resolve. This was never about just one merger: this was about fighting back against corrupt oligarch billionaires trampling the interests of everyday people to line their own pockets." articles.title: Sonu Nigam's new property deal: Singer buys three commercial units in Mumbai's Andheri West for Rs 17 crore - Report
articles.summary: Sonu Nigam has bought three commercial units in Mumbai's Andheri West for a combined Rs 17 crore.
articles.body: Sonu Nigam has bought three commercial units in Mumbai's Andheri West for a combined Rs 17 crore. The deals were registered on August 6, 2026, and the details come from property registration documents.Details of Sonu Nigam's Andheri West purchaseAccording to the documents obtained by CRE Matrix, the units are in the Aston building in the Sundervan Complex on Lokhandwala Road. Two of them are adjoining commercial units on the first floor, while the third is an office on the ground floor.As per the documents, Sonu bought the two first-floor units from Singular Health Private Limited for Rs 16 crore. Together, they have a carpet area of 3,885.77 sq ft. The deal carried a stamp duty of Rs 96 lakh and also included four car parking spaces in the stack parking system in the building's basement.In a separate deal registered the same day, he bought the ground-floor office from the same seller for Rs 1 crore. It has a carpet area of 258.33 sq ft, and the stamp duty paid was Rs 6 lakh.Taken together, the three units have a carpet area of 4,144.10 sq ft, and the total value comes to Rs 17 crore. This works out to roughly Rs 41,021 per sq ft of carpet area. Sonu Nigam and Singular Health Private Limited could not be reached for a comment.Sonu Nigam's other real estate dealsThe singer has been in the news for several property deals over the last two years, including office spaces and land.In May 2026, he sold 1.067 hectares of land in Karjat, part of Mumbai 3.0, for Rs 95 lakh. In April 2026, he sold multiple land parcels totalling over 1.9 hectares in Karjat, a hill station in Raigad district near Mumbai, for Rs 1.95 crore. Both details are based on documents seen by CRE Matrix.In February 2026, his father, Agam Kumar Nigam, bought a 1,197 sq m land parcel in Mumbai's Madh Island for Rs 10 crore. The plot comes with a ground-plus-one-floor residential and commercial structure, according to documents seen by Liases Foras.In 2025, Sonu leased a commercial property in Santacruz East for five years at a total rent of over Rs 12.61 crore. The 4,257 sq ft office is in a building named Trade Centre BKC. It was leased to Pattni Hospitality, which runs a cafe and bar brand called Downtown 29. articles.title: Jeffrey Archer: Best-selling author and former politician dies aged 86
articles.summary: His last book, Adam and Eve, is set to release this month.
articles.body:
Bestselling author and former politician Jeffrey Archer has died at the age of 86.

Archer sold more than 300 million books in his five-decade writing career, including the Clifton Chronicles and Kane and Abel, and often set the novels in his home town of Wellington, Somerset.

In a statement, Archer's publisher HarperCollins said the author died "suddenly and peacefully at home" on Monday between writing sessions.

The former Conservative MP was jailed for perjury in 2001 after being found guilty of lying and cheating in his 1987 libel case against the Daily Star.

Jeffrey Archer obituary: successful novelist, disgraced politician and convicted liar

Archer was born in north London on 15 April 1940 but would quickly move to Weston-super-Mare in Somerset, where his family bought a house from John Cleese's mother.

In 1969, Archer was elected MP for the Lincolnshire constituency of Louth.

He served as an MP for five years before becoming Conservative Party deputy chairman.

His political career was paused in 2001 when he was jailed for four years for perjury and perverting the course of justice.

He was found to have lied in libel action he had brought against The Star newspaper, in which he was awarded £500,000 in damages.

He was released in 2003 and returned to the House of Lords until he retired in 2024.

His last book, Adam and Eve, is set to be released this week, HarperCollins added, describing him as a "master storyteller" whose readers "meant everything to him".

"It's wonderful to come back. What I got a real thrill about when I was walking towards the library is seeing the young boys and girls and thinking, 'that's the next generation'," Archer said at Wellington School.

Archer was due to attend the Cheltenham Festival on Saturday to discuss final his novel.

He and his wife Mary had celebrated their 60th wedding anniversary this year, HarperCollins said.

The pair have two sons and five grandchildren.

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch described Archer's death as a "huge shock".

Writing on X, she said: "I am incredibly saddened to hear this news. He had sent me a lovely message just this morning and was always a great source of encouragement to me personally."

Paying tribute to the bestselling author, Kate Elton, HarperCollins UK CEO and Jeffrey's editor, said: "It has been one of the great privileges of my publishing life to have been Jeffrey Archer's editor.

"He was the master storyteller and an editor's dream - phenomenally hard-working, utterly committed to completing draft after draft to get every word as perfect as possible, and a true champion of the 'team' nature of great publishing."

HarperCollins said the author had been at the Leicester Square Theatre in London on Sunday, signing books for fans with broadcaster Gyles Brandreth.

Writing on X, Brandreth said: "Just yesterday I did a show with Jeffrey Archer to celebrate his new novel – he said it was to be his last.

"He was in the most wonderful, ebullient form and had such a great reception from a packed house. He was funny, engaging and self-deprecating – a great storyteller to the last."

Former Conservative chancellor Nadhim Zahawi paid tribute to the bestselling author on X, describing him as a "dear friend and extraordinary human being".

He wrote: "His gift for storytelling was matched by his wit, warmth and boundless energy. Life was never dull in Jeffrey's company."

articles.title: The Blue Planet and Gandhi composer George Fenton dies aged 76
articles.summary: The musician received five Oscar nominations, and soundtracked dozens of memorable nature films.
articles.body:
Composer George Fenton, whose work included music for films such as Gandhi, Groundhog Day and The Fisher King, as well as TV shows like Planet Earth and Bergerac, has died at the age of 76.

The prolific musician received five Oscar nominations for his film scores, including those for The Remains of the Day and Cry Freedom.

His work on the BBC TV show Blue Planet also earned awards from the Baftas, Emmy Awards and Ivor Novellos; and he also composed theme music for BBC News programmes such as Newsnight and Breakfast Time.

In a statement, Fenton's family said: "We are very sad to announce that George Fenton passed away unexpectedly today."

They continued: "He is survived by his loving wife Amanda, ex-wife Jane, children Gemma, Grace and Bridget, and grandchildren Lola, Audrey, Alfred, George, Frank and Beatrice, and a life of music."

Fenton was born George Howe in Bromley, Kent in 1949. According to a biography on his official website, his father was a mechanical engineer, and his mother had been a dancer before becoming a nurse during the war.

Both parents were musical - his father played drums and his mother played piano - but Fenton chose the electric guitar as his instrument at the age of seven.

That was "when music became more important than football," he later told The Express newspaper. "The Beatles had a huge influence on me."

He took his first lessons from a musician called Brian Rudd.

"He came into our lives as a chimney sweep, which he clearly wasn't," Fenton later recalled.

"My mother went mad at him because he filled the house with soot.

"As he left he said, 'I'm really sorry – but I tuned the boy's guitar for you.' She suggested that as compensation for the mess he could give me a lesson, which he did and then carried on doing."

Later, Fenton began to study the church organ, but rejected the chance to attend university and music college to pursue a career as a performer.

In 1968, he appeared in Alan Bennett's first West End play Forty Years On and was forced to adopt his mother's maiden name, as union rules prevented two actors from having the same name.

During that production, he also understudied the musical director of the show, Carl Davis - who similarly became a prominent composer for film and television.

A year later, he signed a record deal, and scored a top 10 hit in Sweden with a cover of The Beatles' Maxwell's Silver Hammer, but his career as a solo artist was short lived.

In the mid-1970s, he had a recurring role as soldier Martin Gimbel in the ITV soap opera Emmerdale Farm.

But as time went on, he found that directors were always casting him in roles that required him to play an instrument, so he decided to make music his main focus.

Fenton got his first job as composer and musical director for a production of Twelfth Night at the Royal Shakespeare Company in Stratford-upon-Avon in 1974.

Eight years later, he was nominated for an Oscar for his score for Richard Attenborough's Gandhi, on which he worked with Indian composer and instrumentalist Ravi Shankar to develop a score reflecting the country's musical traditions.

It was only his fourth attempt at film music, and he was still almost entirely self-taught.

Throughout the 1980s, he wrote the soundtrack for a number of TV series, including the Bafta-winning The Jewel in the Crown, The Monocled Mutineer, and Alan Bennett's Talking Heads.

He also wrote many well-known theme tunes, including the BBC's One O'Clock News, Six O'Clock News, Nine O'Clock News, Newsnight, The Money Programme, and Radio 4's PM Programme.

For 1987's Cry Freedom - the story of South African campaigner Steve Biko, who was brutally killed by police - he worked with South African jazz musician Jonas Gwangwa, earning two Oscar nominations for best original score and song.

Almost by accident, the title track featured Fenton singing a list of anti-apartheid activists imprisoned or killed by the South African government.

He'd initially recorded the lyrics as a guide for Gwangwa - but the musician decided to keep some of them intact "as a gesture of brotherhood".

"Then it got nominated for an Oscar, so I then found myself singing it on live television to about a billion people, which was not what I intended at all," Fenton later told Radio 4's Desert Island Discs.

After composing the score for the BBC's Trials of Life in 1990, Fenton went on to create the music for what became known as David Attenborough's Earth Trilogy: The Blue Planet, Planet Earth and Frozen Planet.

Fenton's music perfectly complemented the stunning visuals of the ocean's depths and the polar ice caps, adding an emotional weight to the narrative, using the full might of the orchestra to evoke everything from wonder and awe to tension and suspense.

Following the success of the documentaries, Fenton created a show - The Blue Planet in Concert - which has been performed by leading orchestras in venues around the world.

Among his other well-known soundtracks were The Long Walk Home, You've Got Mail, Sweet Home Alabama, The Lady In The Van and Mrs Henderson Presents.

Fenton also scored more films for British director Ken Loach than any other composer.

Their 18 collaborations included Ladybird, Ladybird; I, Daniel Blake and The Wind That Shakes the Barley, which won the Palme d'Or at the 2006 Cannes Film Festival.

He also founded the Association of Professional Composers, which later merged with The Ivors Academy; and he is one of only a handful of musicians to receive the Academy's fellowship, alongside Sir Andrew Lloyd Webber, Sir Elton John, Kate Bush, Bruce Springsteen and George Michael.

In addition, Fenton was a visiting professor at the Royal College of Music and the University of Nottingham. He was made a CBE for services to music in 2023.

The composer often said that his musical career had been an accident, but nothing gave him greater joy than seeing his work come to life.

On his episode of Desert Island Discs, Fenton chose one of his own compositions - Reunion, from the soundtrack to the movie Accidental Hero - as it reminded him of watching pianist John Lowe play the melody in the studio.

"If I was sitting on a desert island and thinking about what a good time I'd had writing music, which I have, I want just one thing to remind me about the best part - which is the fact that you write something and then you're so surprised and thrilled at the way it's played," he told Sue Lawley.

"For a composer, that's the biggest kick you can get."

articles.title: We shot the last film to be made in 'Scotland's Chernobyl'
articles.summary: Sci-fi horror comedy, Behind, features scenes filmed in Port Glasgow's Clune Park shortly before it was demolished.
articles.body:
A short film has captured some of the last images of a derelict housing estate nicknamed "Scotland's Chernobyl" before demolition crews moved in.

The tenements at Clune Park in Port Glasgow were built a century ago as housing for shipyard workers but most of the buildings lay empty for years.

Glasgow-based filmmaker Alessio Avezzano shot scenes for his post-apocalyptic sci-fi horror comedy, Behind, on the estate before bulldozers moved in last May.

"It's the last film to be made there. It was announced it would be demolished the day we were filming - we managed to get in there not a moment too soon," said the Scottish-Italian writer and director.

Redevelopment of Clune Park had been delayed for years due to a stand-off between private landlords and the local council, leaving the site frozen in time with just a handful of tenants remaining.

Large parts of the site became run-down and comparisons were made with the Ukrainian city of Pripyat, abandoned after the 1986 explosion at the Chernobyl nuclear plant led to a huge radiation leak.

The plot for Behind was inspired by "butt dialling", accidentally calling someone from a phone placed in a back pocket.

In the film, it has devastating consequences.

Avezzano said he come up with the idea while trying to write a script.

"That week my cousin, who hadn't done this before or since, just started to butt dial me every day and by the fifth day the light bulb moment came," he said.

"It is basically taking the idea of butt dials and what if they were a symptom of something more deadly."

Avezzano added: "It's got elements of how we responded to the pandemic and it's got elements of phone addiction and social media addiction."

Avezzano said Clune Park gave him the ideal backdrop for the short, and scenes were shot in areas accessible to the public.

Scenes for 2013's sci-fi horror Under the Skin, starring Scarlett Johansson, were also filmed at the estate.

"The idea it was described as Scotland's Chernobyl has always been fascinating." said Avezzano, who is working on his first feature - Midgies - a horror film set in Scotland and due to be released next year.

The lead character is played by Jade McDonald who was in the female run of Singin' I'm No a Billy He's a Tim, a play about a Celtic fan and a Rangers fan locked in a prison cell together on the day of an Old Firm match.

Behind has been taken on a tour of international film festivals, including in Italy and Argentina, following its premiere at Glasgow Film Festival's Frightfest.

It was nominated for the best editing prize at Basingstoke's Exit 6 Film Festival and won best international short at Roswell Shorts Festival in New Mexico.

articles.summary: Caleb Flynn, a former music pastor in Ohio who appeared briefly on \"American Idol\" was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole
articles.body: Caleb Flynn, a former music pastor in Ohio who appeared briefly on "American Idol" was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole Monday after a jury convicted him of murdering his wife while he was having an affair.Caleb Flynn stages wife's murderProsecutors said Caleb Flynn, 40, staged a home invasion in February after shooting Ashley Flynn, a 37-year-old schoolteacher and volleyball coach, then claimed she was killed by a burglar.In his 2013 appearance on "American Idol," Flynn told TV viewers about how his wife had encouraged him to chase his dreams on the singing competition. He did not advance to the main competition in Hollywood.Caleb Flynn apologises in courtWith tears rolling down his cheeks, Flynn apologized in court to his family, starting with his two daughters."I made vows to Ashley on our wedding day. I failed in those vows," he said.Caleb Flynn claims innocenseAlthough he admitted he lied about many things, Flynn remained adamant that he was innocent."As I stand here before God, who is my ultimate judge, I am not lying when I say I did not kill my wife," he said.Miami County Common Pleas Judge Jeannine Pratt said she was deeply disturbed that Flynn used his faith to hide his "deceit" and "lust."She quoted a victim statement from one of the daughters, read aloud moments earlier by a family member, asking: "What did Ashley ever do to make you hate her so much?"Caleb Flynn's text messages to lover shown in courtDuring closing arguments, prosecutors told jurors that Flynn wanted out of his marriage when he shot his wife at their house in Tipp City, a suburb north of Dayton. The couple's two daughters were home with their father when police arrived.He sent a text message to his lover the night before the shooting, saying, "I choose you. I'm free. Actions will come tomorrow," prosecutors said.During the trial, Alleigha Botner testified she met Flynn in 2022 while she was a 20-year-old intern at his church and had an affair with him for more than a year. She told jurors that Flynn said he hated his wife and had thoughts of killing her.Jurors also heard AI-generated love songs that prosecutors said he made for Botner. Flynn didn't testify on his own behalf, nor did anybody else.Gun used in crime 'not found'The gun used to kill Ashley Flynn was not found at the scene, and his attorney told jurors that investigators found no evidence that Caleb Flynn fired a gun that day. Prosecutors said his fingerprints and DNA were at the scene and that his devices showed him moving around the house, even though he claimed he was asleep at the time of the shooting.The jury found him guilty of murder, felonious assault and tampering with evidence.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Debra Messing ditches Democrat for Trump-backed Republican as she sounds alarm over New York
articles.summary: Debra Messing endorsed Republican Bruce Blakeman for New York governor, citing affordability, congestion pricing and the city's economic decline.
articles.body:
Debra Messing has endorsed Republican Bruce Blakeman in the New York governor's race, marking a significant departure from her past support for Democratic candidates.

Messing cited concerns about the economic and social decline of New York City as a key reason for backing Blakeman, emphasizing the need for more affordable living conditions in the city.

Blakeman, who is supported by President Donald Trump, is running against Democratic incumbent Gov. Kathy Hochul, with issues like affordability, taxes, crime, and immigration at the forefront of his campaign.

Debra Messing has had enough with the state of New York.

The "Will & Grace" actress snubbed Democratic incumbent Gov. Kathy Hochul and instead threw her support behind Republican Bruce Blakeman in the New York governor's race.

The endorsement marked a striking political shift for Messing, who has campaigned for Democratic candidates in the past. She previously backed Hillary Clinton in 2016 and Cynthia Nixon's 2018 bid for New York governor.

Messing has also publicly clashed with President Donald Trump , a supporter of Blakeman.

Her past political allegiances appeared to take a back seat as Messing enthusiastically praised Blakeman's campaign for governor.

"Oh gosh, I am so grateful that you are running," she told Blakeman in a video shared on Instagram . "You are what we need more than anything."

"The decline in this city over the last four years has been so exponential and devastating economically, socially on every level, and obviously we've lost so much business here. People are leaving the city."

Fox News Digital reached out to Messing's representative for comment.

The "Wedding Date" star, a New York native, said her support for Blakeman was rooted in concerns about the direction of the city and the financial pressures facing residents.

"I was born here. This is the city I love, and it's not the city that I love anymore, and I believe with all my heart that you are the answer," she added.

"You are the affordable candidate and I think, more than anything, people are just really struggling, and they need their utilities to be lower, and they don't want to have to pay to have congestion and the driving."

Messing said affordability was at the heart of her concerns, pointing to the growing financial burden she believes New Yorkers are being forced to shoulder.

"It's just too expensive to live in New York City and I love the fact that that is the top of your mind," she added.

Blakeman currently serves as Nassau County executive and is the Republican nominee for governor of New York in the 2026 election. He has challenged Democratic New York Gov. Kathy Hochul in the race, with affordability, taxes, crime and immigration at the center of his campaign.

articles.summary: Salman Khan’s upcoming war drama 'Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace' has undergone yet another round of significant changes, with the makers reportedly
articles.body: Salman Khan’s upcoming war drama 'Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace' has undergone yet another round of significant changes, with the makers reportedly revisiting both the film’s climax and the actor’s character arc ahead of its Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) screening. According to a report by Mid-Day, director Apoorva Lakhia and the writing team have reworked the ending to align with the film’s evolving tone and its emphasis on peace. The film, which began as 'Battle of Galwan', has already gone through extensive changes in its story, title and treatment following shifts in India-China relations.Salman Khan’s 'Maatrubhumi' gets a reworked climax and character arcWith 'Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace' reportedly set to be viewed by the CBFC this week, the makers have made further alterations to the Salman Khan-starrer.As reported by Mid-Day, the film’s climax has been rewritten and Salman’s character arc has also been modified. The changes are said to reflect the film’s revised approach towards the India-China conflict and its broader message of peace.A source cited by the publication indicated that the makers have been particularly careful about how the conflict is portrayed. The revised ending is reportedly designed to complement the film’s emphasis on reconciliation and peace rather than simply concluding on a conventional war-drama note.'Maatrubhumi' gets Ministry of Information and Broadcasting clearanceThe film's revised version reportedly received a No Objection Certificate from the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting last week. According to the Mid-Day report, the movie has subsequently been submitted to the CBFC, with the makers now awaiting a screening date. If the film is examined by the censor board this week as expected, the certification process could provide greater clarity on its eventual release plans.The CBFC review will also mark an important stage for a project that has undergone multiple rounds of rewriting and reshooting since it was first announced.The production team was contacted by Mid-Day for a response but had not commented at the time of publication.How did the film evolve from 'Battle of Galwan' to 'Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace'?The Salman Khan starrer was initially announced as 'Battle of Galwan', with the story centred on the 2020 India-China clash in the Galwan Valley. Khan was reportedly set to portray Colonel Bikumalla Santosh Babu, the Indian Army officer who was involved in the confrontation. However, the film's treatment subsequently underwent considerable changes. With India-China relations evolving in the years since the Galwan clash, concerns reportedly emerged around how the neighbouring country and the conflict would be depicted on screen.The project was consequently reworked and reshot, eventually emerging under the new title 'Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace'. The change in title also signalled a shift in the film's overall tonality and thematic positioning.Salman Khan’s current work slate'Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace', directed by Apoorva Lakhia, stars Salman Khan alongside Chitrangda Singh. Salman Khan is currently filming Vamshi Paidipally's action entertainer, tentatively titled 'Monster', opposite Nayanthara. Produced by Dil Raju under Sri Venkateswara Creations, the project is aiming for an Eid 2027 theatrical debut. The actor will juggle his 'Bigg Boss 20' hosting duties alongside the shoot before shifting his complete attention to his upcoming project with Raj & DK towards the end of the year.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: Shehnaaz Gill discusses her experiences in Bollywood, the impact of language barriers, and the lessons learned from her initial haste in selecting film roles. Discover her thoughts on impactful roles and the advice given by Salman Khan.
articles.body: Shehnaaz Gill knows that her Bollywood journey could have taken a different turn. The popularity she gained with Bigg Boss 13 opened the doors to Hindi cinema, but the projects that followed did not give her the kind of roles she was looking for. She now admits she picked up projects in haste and says she has learnt to be more selective. Excerpts from a conversation...‘There is a language barrier when it comes to me in Bollywood’Shehnaaz believes that language could be one of the reasons she has not been approached for more Hindi films. She says, “I think there is a language barrier when it comes to me in Bollywood, which is why I feel makers don’t approach me. But they’ve never seen the kind of actor I am. When they figure that out, I’m sure things will change.”Talking about several South actors making a mark in Hindi cinema, she says, “Is there anything stopping South actors? They are working. It is all about chadhte suraj ko salaam karte hai... toh hum Punjab se suraj Mumbai chadhayenge aur inko batayenge.”Shehnaaz has also continued to work in Punjabi cinema, where she has turned producer. She headlined and produced Ikk Kudi, which released in 2025, and was more recently, was seen in Singh vs Kaur 2 with Gippy Grewal.‘You learn from your mistakes’Looking back at her acting career, Shehnaaz says, “You can say that I picked up projects in haste initially. I didn’t do impactful roles. If I had done that, people would see me with a different perspective. Maine script choose karne mein hurry kar di. But you learn from your mistakes. I am getting more mature now. There should be something for you to do in a film. If there is nothing, then it’s pointless. The audience is going to watch the film for you, right? They shouldn’t be disappointed.”But her first Bollywood outing, Kisi Ka Bhai Kisi Ki Jaan, which gave her an opportunity to work with Salman Khan, comes without regrets. “That was a fun film and I was happy to be part of it. Salman sir had told me that after this film, take up impactful roles. articles.summary: Discover Johnny Depp's insights into his creative process in the latest documentary 'Unleashed Spirits: The Rise of the Hollywood Vampires,' where he discusses writing music and the journey of his rock supergroup with Alice Cooper and Joe Perry.
articles.body: Johnny Depp is well known for his on-screen prowess in films like ‘Charlie and the Chocolate Factory,' ‘Pirates of the Caribbean,' ‘Edward Scissorhands,' and many others. However, did you know that he has also dabbled in music? In 2012, Depp, along with Alice Cooper and Joe Perry, started their own rock music supergroup, the Hollywood Vampires. Depp recently opened up about his music background in a clip from the documentary ‘Unleashed Spirits: The Rise of the Hollywood Vampires,' which chronicles the group’s journey from just starting out to gaining international fame.Johnny Depp talks about the Hollywood Vampires and his journey in musicComingSoon.net recently released footage from the documentary ‘Unleashed Spirits: The Rise of the Hollywood Vampires.' In the clip, Depp opened up about writing songs, specifically touching upon writing ‘This Is a Song’ for Miss Hedy Lamarr. He shared, “It’s about if the inspiration hits, if the words pop into your head, how much time do you have before they fall out?” Depp also admitted that he always keeps a notebook on him since he is completely unaware of when the inspiration may strike again.The clip also featured scenes from 2018, when the star was working in his music studio late at night. He was also filmed playing the piano late into the night, as Tony Henrikson, another band member, narrated in the background, explaining Depp’s creative process.The documentary on the Hollywood Vampires was directed by Daniel E. articles.title: 'Ramayana' actor Sunil Lahri warns of drought and shortages; asks people to cut consumption by 15-20%; cites El Nino; says 'it is a matter of being smart'
articles.summary: Actor Sunil Lahri has urged people to conserve essential resources amid concerns over drought, water shortages and changing weather patterns.
articles.body: Actor Sunil Lahri has urged people to conserve essential resources amid concerns over drought, water shortages and changing weather patterns. The actor, best known for playing Lakshman in the 1987 television serial 'Ramayan', shared a video message on social media.Sunil Lahri spoke about the El Nino phenomenon and its possible impact on rainfall, agriculture and the availability of essential commodities. He described the situation as a warning that requires people to be cautious rather than afraid.Sunil Lahri urges people to conserve resourcesSunil Lahri said changing weather conditions could create serious challenges for several Asian countries. He warned that prolonged drought could affect water supplies and agricultural production.The actor also raised concerns about fertilizers and other necessities becoming harder to obtain. He pointed out that money may not be enough if essential commodities themselves become scarce."The time has come for us to save everything little by little," Sunil Lahri said. He asked people to reduce their overall consumption by around 15-20%. His appeal covered several everyday necessities, including food, oil, petrol and diesel.Maharashtra faces rainfall shortageSunil Lahri's comments come amid concerns over drought and deficient rainfall in Maharashtra. The rainfall shortage has already affected agricultural activity across several parts of the state.Many regions have reported crop damage following inadequate rainfall. Maharashtra reportedly received around 19% less rainfall than its seasonal average between June and September. As many as 21 districts were also reported to have received deficient rainfall.Authorities in the state have stepped up water-conservation measures as concerns over availability continue.Actor compares warning with COVID-19 crisisWhile discussing the possibility of a future resource crisis, Sunil Lahri referred to the COVID-19 pandemic. He recalled how people managed to face the challenges posed by the pandemic.The actor said a similar approach could help people deal with another major crisis. He stressed that preparation should begin before shortages become more serious."During COVID, we fought and came out without crying. In the same way, I am sure we will also come out of this disaster.It is not a matter of being scared; it is a matter of being smart. It is a matter of being careful. It is a warning. Therefore, we have to try to cut 15-20% in everything, including food, oil, petrol and diesel."Sunil Lahri asks people to act before crisis hitsSunil Lahri further emphasized the importance of taking precautions at an early stage. He suggested that people should not wait for a major shortage before changing their consumption habits. He used the possibility of a fire as an analogy for the warning signs he believes are already visible. According to the actor, acting early could help people avoid the worst consequences.He added, "So, I am sure we will come out of this disaster. It is said that when there is a fire, the smoke is lost. Looking at the possibility of a fire, the smoke is already lost. Therefore, if we are already careful, then we will not even know when this disaster will happen and when it will happen.What do you think? Be happy, be happy, be healthy. Jai Shri Ram."Sunil Lahri's career after 'Ramayan'Sunil Lahri became a household name through his portrayal of Lakshman in Ramanand Sagar's 'Ramayan'. The 1987 television series went on to become one of the most recognized mythological shows in Indian television history.The actor has continued to remain associated with the character years after the series ended. His last credited feature film appearance was in the 2017 Hindi movie 'A Daughter's Tale: Pankh'.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.standfirst: La actriz se ha destapado como una gran aficionada al 'running'
articles.summary: La actriz se ha destapado como una gran aficionada al 'running'
articles.body: La actriz Amber Heard se ha destapado como una gran aficionada al running. Este fin de semana, participó en la media maratón de San Sebastián y compartió su tiempo con orgullo en las redes sociales. "Primera media maratón. ¡Eskerrik asko Donosti! 21 kilómetros en 1 hora y 39 minutos", publicó en Instagram. En las fotografías, Amber Heard aparece con una enorme cara de satisfacción. Para un corredor popular, un tiempo de 1:39 en una media maratón es un crono notable, ya que implica un ritmo de 4:42 minutos el kilómetro. Está lejos, obviamente, de marcas más avanzadas, pero estamos hablando de alguien, como la actriz estadounidense, que se estrenaba por primera vez en la distancia. Amber Heard finalizó en la posición 830 de la media maratón, de 3.800 personas que la acabaron, como puede observarse en la clasificación oficial de la prueba. La actriz, que lució el dorsal 1.559, se inscribió con su nombre real y no dudó en compartir su alegría en redes. La publicación de Amber Heard en redes sociales ha generado numerosas felicitaciones. La actriz lleva ya tres años viviendo en España. Actualmente reside en el barrio de El Viso, en Madrid, una de las zonas más exclusivas de la ciudad. La artista pasa página en nuestro país del polémico juicio contra su expareja, el también actor Johnny Depp. La estadounidense, de 40 años, perdió el proceso judicial. El keniano Mark Kosgey Kiptoo batió el récord mundial en la media maratón de Donostia en categoría de mayores de 50 años con un tiempo de 1 hora, tres minutos y 57 segundos. La anterior mejor marcar mundial M50 era de 1h06:17. La media maratón de Donostia, que celebró el pasado 3 de octubre su quinta edición, contó con 5.200 inscritos. En clave femenina, la española Maitane Melero fue la gran vencedora de la jornada parando el reloj en 1h15:44.

articles.title: 'Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha' producer takes indirect dig at Ranbir Kapoor and Namit Malhotra's 'Ramayana' team for ‘negative marketing' amid poor box office performance and re-release plans: ‘We never got a chance to reach our audience’
articles.summary: 'Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha' producer Prakash Mahobiya has alleged that the film faced a deliberate negative marketing campaign amid the buzz
articles.body: 'Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha' producer Prakash Mahobiya has alleged that the film faced a deliberate negative marketing campaign amid the buzz surrounding Nitesh Tiwari’s 'Ramayana', starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash. The producer claimed that YouTubers and influencers were allegedly encouraged to spread negative information about his film. As 'Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha' prepares for a re-release, Mahobiya has opened up about its poor box office performance and the circumstances surrounding its theatrical run.Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha producer alleges negative PR'Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha' was released in theatres on September 25, ahead of Nitesh Tiwari’s much-awaited 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, which stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. However, the mythological film faced criticism even before its theatrical release, particularly over its casting and visual effects.Speaking to India Today, producer Prakash Mahobiya addressed the film's poor box office performance and alleged that the negative buzz surrounding it was not entirely organic. According to Mahobiya, the film was subjected to a negative marketing campaign involving YouTubers, influencers and others.“It was negative marketing throughout. We never got a chance to reach our audience. The ones who watched our film really enjoyed it. But if they never got to see it, how will they even have an opinion?” he said.Producer hints at another big-budget film on the same subjectWhile Mahobiya did not directly name 'Ramayana', he referred to an upcoming big-budget film based on the same epic. Nitesh Tiwari's 'Ramayana', backed by Namit Malhotra, is among the most anticipated Indian films and is scheduled to arrive during Diwali 2026.Mahobiya claimed that his team was told that negative information about 'Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha' was being circulated because another film on the same subject was in the pipeline.“From what we have been told, there are other movies on the same subject coming in, the big-budget film. As far as we know, a lot of negative marketing opportunities have been given to YouTubers, influencers and other people. They are spreading wrong information and asking people not to watch our film,” he alleged.When asked specifically whether he was accusing the teams behind Nitesh Tiwari's 'Ramayana' and Namit Malhotra, Mahobiya stopped short of making a direct allegation.“I don’t know for sure, but that’s what we are being told,” he said.The producer's comments are an allegation, and no evidence establishing that the 'Ramayana' team organised or directed such a campaign has been presented in the statements quoted above.'Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha' faced backlash before releaseDirected by Abhishek Singh, Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha stars Anjali Arora, Dev Sharma and Rajneish Duggal in key roles. Anjali plays Sita in the film. The casting, particularly Anjali's portrayal of Sita, became a subject of discussion and criticism on social media ahead of the release. The film's VFX also drew criticism from sections of the audience.After its September 25 theatrical release, the film continued to face backlash over several aspects of its presentation. One of the scenes that attracted attention showed a member of the Vanar Sena wearing spectacles, which prompted further reactions online.According to Sacnilk, 'Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha' collected around Rs. 46 lakh worldwide during its theatrical run.Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha makers plan a re-releaseDespite the film's disappointing theatrical performance, Mahobiya has indicated that the makers are looking at giving 'Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha' another opportunity to reach audiences. The producer maintained that the response from viewers who actually watched the film was encouraging and suggested that the movie's limited reach was one of the major reasons for its box office failure.The planned re-release comes at a time when anticipation around big-screen adaptations of the Ramayana remains high, particularly with Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana set to bring together Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and a large ensemble cast.Ranbir Kapoor's Ramayana is gearing up for Diwali 2026 releaseNitesh Tiwari's 'Ramayana' is one of the most ambitious Indian mythological projects currently in production. The film stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, while Yash plays Ravana. The project is backed by Namit Malhotra and has generated considerable interest because of its scale, visual effects and star cast.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Celtic Connections reveals 2027 festival programme
articles.summary: The 34th edition of the folk, roots and world music event will run from 14 January until 31 January.
articles.body:
A tribute to the Beatles, a takeover of the Kelvingrove Art Gallery and a special gig by film composer AR Rahman are among the shows unveiled for next year's Celtic Connections festival in Glasgow.

The 34th edition of the folk, roots and world music event will run from 14 January until 31 January and open with a special concert by Scotland's GRIT Orchestra, playing orchestral arrangements of some of well-known folk songs.

Musicians from over 20 countries will perform while a new membership scheme will offer reduced tickets to people under 26.

Last year's festival saw about 114,000 people attend shows across the city.

More stories from Glasgow & West Scotland

The opening concert will be held at the Royal Concert Hall and features the GRIT Orchestra, which was originally assembled over a decade ago to pay tribute to the late folk musician Martyn Bennett.

It will play new arrangements of both ancient and contemporary folk tunes to launch the 2027 festival.

Slumdog Millionaire composer Rahman will perform at the Glasgow International Arena - formerly known as the Emirates Arena - in collaboration with British talents Rushil Ranjan and Abi Sampa.

It will be the first time the show, which bridges the gap between Western and Indian classical music, is performed in the UK outside of London.

Festival mainstay the Roaming Roots Revue will have a Beatles theme this year, with guests to be announced performing tracks from the band's back catalogue, backed by an orchestra and live band.

Other gigs include Heartbeats singer José González, folk-rock band the Saw Doctors, Pogues collaborator Iona Zajac, and Irish accordionist Sharon Shannon, who will be joined by Sir Bob Geldof.

Tribute shows to Joni Mitchell, Glasgow folk singer Matt McGinn, and British folk-rock singer Sandy Denny will also feature.

Scottish folk singer Karine Polwart will host two nights of shows called Curiosity Cabinet at Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, with songs and melodies based around some of the objects.

The Tall Ship Glenlee will also be used as a venue for the first time.

Festival director Donald Shaw told BBC Scotland News it was important the event tried to offer affordable tickets, despite rising costs.

"I think everyone is in the same boat in terms of challenges with logistical costs, production costs, and travel costs. We have to balance having a sensible budget with keeping an ambitious programme.

"We want to include as many people as possible and what we are trying to do is put any funding we get for Celtic Connections into keeping ticket prices at a reasonable level and offer discounts for a younger generation."

The festival director, who has been in post for over 20 years, said he believes the festival's eclectic approach has helped it reach more diverse audiences in recent years.

"Over the last decade there has been such a natural evolution of folk music, and we have seen crossover with orchestral music, jazz, electronica and world music.

"It has meant Celtic Connections is more colourful than ever. The scene itself is wider now, and I think the availability of music digitally and through social media has meant trad music and folk itself is even more widespread.

"It's a great thing and there is a sense of confidence within the music scene in Scotland now."

Among the acts booked are Beoga, the Irish folk band who recently quit Ed Sheeran's tour in support of support act Macklemore, who was dropped from the tour over pro-Palestine comments.

Shaw said folk music has always had political elements to it.

"We are always keen to let the artist have their voice and have their say. That's been the backbone of folk music culture for 50 or 60 years at least."

Tickets for the festival go on sale this Thursday.

articles.title: Dolly Parton estate battle: Country singer’s nephew accused of using barbed wire and caution tape to evade lawsuit service
articles.summary: A new development has emerged in the legal dispute surrounding the estate of late country music icon Dolly Parton.
articles.body: A new development has emerged in the legal dispute surrounding the estate of late country music icon Dolly Parton. Lawyers representing her estate claim that her nephew Bryan Seaver appeared to take unusual measures to prevent process servers from delivering legal papers to him, including placing caution tape and barbed wire across the entrance to his home.The allegation was made in a recent court filing by She’s Alive LLC, the entity established to manage and protect Parton’s business interests after her death. The estate’s lawyers were responding to Seaver’s request for additional time to find an attorney ahead of a hearing concerning a temporary restraining order against him.According to the filing, attempts were made three times to serve Seaver with the lawsuit. During one visit, a process server reportedly saw four cars in the driveway but received no response at the front door. The estate says that on a later attempt, a “no trespassing” sign had appeared in the yard, while barbed wire was allegedly placed across the handrails leading to the front entrance.The estate also submitted a photograph that appeared to show barbed wire stretched across the railings of Seaver’s porch, along with strips of yellow caution tape. However, the filing only alleges that these measures were intended to prevent service; there has been no court finding that Seaver installed them specifically for that purpose.The latest dispute is part of a larger legal battle that began after Seaver, who had worked as Parton’s head of security, was accused by She’s Alive of making threatening statements toward people connected to the singer’s estate and business interests. A Tennessee judge previously granted the estate a temporary restraining order, requiring Seaver and his security company to stay away from estate property and remain at least 1,000 feet from its employees and business partners.Court documents cited by the estate include messages in which Seaver allegedly threatened to damage Parton’s brand and discussed launching a podcast aimed at her business partnerships. The judge said the alleged communications were concerning because they were accompanied by demands for payment and references to Seaver’s claimed access to weapons and experience with violence.Seaver has denied that his messages were threats. In a statement previously given to the media, he said his comments had been taken out of context and described them as private conversations with people he considered friends. He also said Parton had jokingly referred to him as her “killer.”The estate’s latest filing argues that Seaver should not receive additional time to prepare his defense because, according to its lawyers, he had already attempted to avoid being served with the lawsuit. A hearing regarding the restraining order is currently scheduled for October 9, although that date could change if the court grants Seaver’s request for more time to obtain legal representation.The legal fight comes just weeks after Parton died on August 25, 2026, at the age of 80. Seaver was the family member who publicly announced her death in a video shared through Parton’s social media accounts.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.body: Superstar Rajinikanth will next be seen in the much awaited sequel ‘Jailer 2’ helmed by Nelson Dilipkumar. Ahead of the film’s theatrical release on October 15, there’s huge excitement among the fans. After releasing the trailer, the makers seem to have taken a different approach to promotions this time. Instead of the grand audio launch usually associated with his films, the makers have opted for a low-key album launch followed by a rare three-hour television interview with the legendary star.‘Jailer 2’ to skip the traditional audio launchAs per India Today, the special interview is scheduled for October 11 and will air on Sun TV from 6:30 pm to 9:30 pm. The three-hour appearance comes just four days before ‘Jailer 2’ releases worldwide on October 15.Rajinikanth’s audio launches have often become major promotional events. His speeches, personal anecdotes and composer Anirudh Ravichander’s live performances usually generate significant attention.However, ‘Jailer 2’ has moved away from that familiar format. Instead of organising a large audio launch with the cast and crew, the makers unveiled the album through a more private event.The music was launched at "Jailer 2 RAVE", an event organised for selected fans.
